summary: Physics, Chinese historiography and economic thought receive direct evidence. Smith scholarship and reader disagreement distinguish historical importance from present-day use. Sima Qian's full-English-edition eligibility remains unresolved.
next: Verify complete Euclid/Newton/Smith editions, broaden other nonfiction fields, and investigate Sima Qian translation completeness before eligibility.

sources.title: Principia
sources.author: Keith Moore
sources.note: Describes the 1687 manuscript and publication, including the three-book structure and Halley’s contribution; situates the work’s laws of motion and gravity in scientific reception.
sources.limits: Institutional commemorative essay, not a full critical analysis of mathematical arguments.

targets.A: Physics candidate and work-boundary evidence expands all-subject coverage.
targets.N: History-of-science evidence supports inclusion, without assuming modern textbook usefulness.

sources.title: The Recent Scholarship on Adam Smith’s The Wealth of Nations: A Review
sources.publisher: The Japanese Society for the History of Economic Thought / J-STAGE
sources.author: Keiichi Watanabe
sources.note: Abstract contrasts economic-history and moral-philosophical approaches, surveying Japanese and international Smith scholarship.
sources.limits: Full PDF unavailable; cited studies not separately consulted.

sources.title: Sima Qian: Records of the Grand Historian
sources.author: Jeremiah Jenne
sources.note: Connects historical method, moral narrative and lasting cultural influence. Identifies Watson’s selective translation and an unfinished Nienhauser project, requiring an explicit English-completeness check.
sources.limits: PDF and web versions are one essay. Its translation-status claim is dated 2025 and must be checked before excluding the work.

targets.A: Chinese historiography expands the comparison universe; eligibility is pending.
targets.N: Supports historical and reading significance while exposing edition limitations.

sources.title: How can I build up enough economic literacy to read The Wealth of Nations?
sources.note: Readers disagree over accessibility and value: several prefer current textbooks, while others praise historical observation and the colonies chapter. Historical importance does not settle present reading priority.
sources.limits: Self-selected forum; credentials and sweeping historical claims unverified. Abridgment recommendations do not meet complete-work eligibility.

targets.A: Direct disagreement helps compare historical standing with reading value.
targets.N: Reader experience tests the case for reading an old economics work today.
